svg.text: go-memdb: restore transactions, queries and watches
HashiCorp's in-memory database has 30 public methods replaced by panics. The agent restores them from the remaining code, the API comments and the README,
so writers commit atomically, readers query consistent snapshots and watchers wake when their results change.
describe every method and its contract
one copy-on-write radix tree per index;
every node has a watch channel
linkname or embed; text Go diffs only
Abort, Commit, Delete, DeletePrefix, DeleteAll, FirstWatch, First,
ReverseLowerBound, Defer, iterator Next and WatchCh,
NewWatchSet, Add, AddWithLimit, Watch, WatchCtx, WatchCh
PrefixFromArgs for string and compound indexes,
74 for the restored methods, 31 index and
reward 1 only if all 105 pass; the patch is
joe + watch channel of that tree node
the old snapshot still returns joe
Commit(): swap in the new tree roots
WatchCtx returns nil: the result changed
then run deferred notify(); Abort() instead would discard the delete
A value received on a watched channel must wake WatchCtx the same way a closed channel does.
ONE TRANSACTION, AS THE RESTORED METHODS MUST HANDLE IT
readers keep a consistent snapshot while a writer commits, and watchers wake when their query result changes
